title: Aerospike Health and Performance Report
text:
⚡ The cluster is stable but showing signs of resource pressure. 3 findings suggest optimization is required.



This diagnostic evaluates the wizd-dev.asdb-dev-pl203979.azure-nonprod.fmrcloud.com environment, currently running Aerospike 7.2.0.8 across a 6-node footprint. Optimized as a Available/Partition-tolerant (AP) deployment, the findings below prioritize throughput efficiency and resource headroom.









Integrity
⚠️ Detected 9 configuration drifts across the cluster.


Capacity
✅ Resource utilization is healthy. Peak consumption is currently 0%.


Security
✅ Connection distribution is healthy. Top user: srvAP156348_INT (54%).

WarningConfig Symmetry

WarningConfig Drift



The static aerospike.conf file was not found in the collectinfo bundle.







As per Rule 2.d, disk utilization is monitored against a 60% High Water Mark (HWM) to prevent forced evictions.


                            
                                            






Rule 6.a monitors connection distribution. Your current audit shows one user holding a significant monopoly on these resources.


                            
                                            






High volumes of fail_key_busy errors indicate extreme write contention on specific records, which can lead to application-level latency and timeouts.



✅ No active hot key contention detected in the recent telemetry window.







The following items were identified as requiring attention to ensure optimal cluster health, performance, and predictability.







Warning1.b | Network Acceleration Check (WARNING)



Observation: System telemetry (sys_stats) is missing from the bundle.
Remediation Action: Why this matters: Without system-level telemetry, we cannot verify if hardware interrupt queues or optimized network drivers (ENA) are active.
Action Plan: 1. Re-run the collection with system metrics enabled: asadm -e "collectinfo". 2. Ensure the user running the command has permissions to execute ethtool, lsmod, and top. 3. If using Docker, ensure the container has visibility into the host network stack.








Warning3.a | Config Symmetry (WARNING)



Observation: Detected 9 configuration drifts across the cluster.
Remediation Action: Why this matters: Asymmetric configurations create silent bottlenecks and unpredictable behavior.
Action Plan: 1. Run asadm -e 'conf diff' to pinpoint the remaining differences. 2. Standardize timeouts, thread counts, and memory limits across all nodes.








Warning3.b | Config Drift (⚠️ DATA MISSING)



Observation: The static aerospike.conf file was not found in the collectinfo bundle.
Remediation Action: Why this matters: We cannot compare live settings against your config file if the file wasn’t bundled.
Action Plan: 1. Re-run collectinfo and explicitly point to your config file: asadm -e "collectinfo --cf /etc/aerospike/aerospike.conf" 2. If your config is in a custom location, update the path in the command above.

cluster_clock_skew > 0.

index-type flash with default sub-configs.

2.b

✅
Object count vs. sprigs ratio > 1:256.
[cite_start]Why: Too few sprigs cause slow record lookups [cite: 79][cite_start].Action: Increase partition-tree-sprigs (requires restart)[cite: 79].

data-used-pct within 5% of defrag-lwm-pct.

data_used_pct > 60%.

[cite_start]Why: Risks OOM killer stopping the process [cite: 84][cite_start].Action: Reduce index RAM or upgrade hardware[cite: 17, 35].

heap-efficiency-pct < 60%.

VERSION STAMP

—————————————————————————–
version = “1.4.0”


— Metadata —


ID: {X.y} (e.g., 1.a) -> Matches the Aerospike Health Catalog


Title: Descriptive Name for the report table
def run_check(db_path=“aerospike_health.db”): conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONFIGURATION
# Set your Rule ID and Name here. These appear in the final report.
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
check_id = "X.y"
check_name = "Descriptive Rule Name"

try:
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. SCHEMA SAFETY CHECK
    # Before querying, we verify the table exists to prevent a crash if 
    # the ingestor failed or the bundle was incomplete.
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    cursor = conn.cursor()
    target_table = "node_stats" # Replace with your required table
    cursor.execute(f"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='{target_table}'")
    
    if not cursor.fetchone():
        return {
            "id": check_id, "name": check_name, "status": "⚠️ DATA MISSING",
            "message": f"Table '{target_table}' not found in database.",
            "remediation": "Verify that the correct Ingestor is enabled in ingest/__init__.py."
        }

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. QUERY LOGIC
    # Use standard SQL. Aim for specific columns rather than SELECT *
    # to keep the dataframe lightweight.
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    query = f"SELECT node_id, metric, value FROM {target_table} WHERE metric = 'example_metric'"
    df = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)
    
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. ANALYSIS & RESULTS
    # Standard PASS/WARNING/CRITICAL logic.
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
    if df.empty:
        return {
            "id": check_id, "name": check_name, "status": "PASS",
            "message": "Healthy state description: e.g., No error skew detected.",
            "remediation": "None"
        }
    
    # Example threshold check (Adjust as needed)
    threshold = 100
    findings = df[df['value'] > threshold]

    if not findings.empty:
        return {
            "id": check_id,
            "name": check_name,
            "status": "WARNING", # Or "CRITICAL"
            "message": f"Detected {len(findings)} nodes exceeding threshold {threshold}.",
            "remediation": (
                "**Why this matters:** [Explain the technical impact].\n\n"
                "**Action Plan:**\n"
                "1. Step-by-step resolution using `asadm`.\n"
                "2. Configuration changes required."
            )
        }

    # Final default fallback
    return {
        "id": check_id, "name": check_name, "status": "PASS",
        "message": "All metrics within normal bounds.", "remediation": "None"
    }
    
except Exception as e:
    # Graceful failure: prevents one bad rule from breaking the whole report
    return {
        "id": check_id, "name": check_name, "status": "CRITICAL",
        "message": f"Execution Error: {str(e)}",
        "remediation": "Review the database schema and rule query logic."
    }
finally:
    conn.close()

title: Aerospike Ingestor Template (v1.0.0)
text:
All ingestors must be Class-based and reside in the ingest/ directory. They are responsible for taking a specific slice of the Aerospike JSON telemetry and persisting it to SQLite.




Signature: Must implement run_ingest(self, node_id, node_data, conn, run_id).
Schema Safety: Must use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS.
Data Integrity: Must use INSERT OR REPLACE to avoid duplication.
Version Stamp: Must include a __version__ string at the top of the file.




import sqlite3

__version__ = "1.x.x"

class YourMetricIngestor:
    def run_ingest(self, node_id, node_data, conn, run_id):
        cursor = conn.cursor()
        
        # 1. Ensure Table Exists
        cursor.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS your_table (
                node_id TEXT,
                metric_name TEXT,
                value REAL,
                PRIMARY KEY (node_id, metric_name)
            )
        """)
        
        # 2. Extract Data from node_data
        # Navigate to your specific JSON path (e.g., node_data['as_stat']['...'])
        target_metrics = node_data.get("as_stat", {}).get("target_key", {})
        
        # 3. Persist
        for key, val in target_metrics.items():
            cursor.execute("""
                INSERT OR REPLACE INTO your_table (node_id, metric_name, value)
                VALUES (?, ?, ?)
            """, (node_id, key, val))

Warning2.b | Sprig Limit Warning (WARNING)

Remediation Action: Why this matters: Sprigs define the number of sub-trees in the primary index. For Index-on-Flash, a low sprig count causes ‘deep’ trees, requiring more disk IOPS per lookup. This can lead to high read latency and SSD saturation.
Action Plan: 1. Increase partition-tree-sprigs in the namespace stanza (e.g., to 4096, 8192, or 16384). 2. Note: This setting requires a cold start of the Aerospike process to rebuild the index.








Warning3.a | Config Symmetry (WARNING)



Observation: Detected 10 configuration drifts across the cluster.
Remediation Action: Why this matters: Asymmetric configurations create silent bottlenecks and unpredictable behavior.
Action Plan: 1. Run asadm -e 'conf diff' to pinpoint the remaining differences. 2. Standardize timeouts, thread counts, and memory limits across all nodes.

Observation: The static aerospike.conf file was not found in the collectinfo bundle.
Remediation Action: Why this matters: We cannot compare live settings against your config file if the file wasn’t bundled.
Action Plan: 1. Re-run collectinfo and explicitly point to your config file: asadm -e "collectinfo --cf /etc/aerospike/aerospike.conf" 2. If your config is in a custom location, update the path in the command above.








Warning6.a | Security Connection Audit (WARNING)



Observation: Connection Monopoly: User [countersUser] holds 87% of cluster connections (1554).
Remediation Action: Assessment: A single user account monopolizing client connections can lead to ‘Service Unavailable’ errors for other applications and administrative tools (asadm/asinfo).
Action Plan: 1. Audit the connection pooling configuration for the application using the countersUser account. 2. Ensure client SDKs are using a max connection limit that aligns with the cluster’s proto-fd-max setting. 3. Check for ‘connection leaks’ in long-running application processes.
